category_title: Students who become expressionless when their intelligence is publicly mocked
scenario_title: Public math problem solving after quiz collection
minimal_context: Javier is called to the board in front of his math class to solve a problem and show his work after quizzes were collected.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Now you got to show your work. Javier, come to the board to solve a problem.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Walks to the board in front of the class to solve the problem.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Go ahead and write out your solution.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Attempts the problem on the board, writing out the steps, but gets the wrong answer.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to do it like you are in kindergarten, that way you make no mistakes, right? Write this 17 times. (Writes "17 times" on the board) Right, Javier?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at the board expressionless, completely withdrawing and silencing himself as an act of protest and disengagement.)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Now you got to show your work. Javier, come to the board to solve a problem.

STUDENT: (Walks to the board in front of the class to solve the problem.)

STUDENT: (Looks at the board expressionless, completely withdrawing and silencing himself as an act of protest and disengagement.)

task.content: Come to the board to solve a problem and "show your work"

context.social_setting: In front of the class, directed to a specific student by the instructor

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: After the student attempts the problem but gets the wrong answer, and the professor uses infantilizing language and public shaming
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Looks at the board expressionless, withdrawal, silencing, disengagement
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Anxiety, depression, anger, feeling disempowered, cognitive distraction ("Did that really just happen?"), activation of stereotype threat ("Do I have to prove myself as a member of my group yet again?")
related_quotes: You need to do it like you are in kindergarten, that way you make no mistakes, right? Write this 17 times [he writes, “17 times” on the board]—Right, Javier?

behavior_patterns.condition: Following a microaggressive event or when instructors use sarcasm and express obvious frustration
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Disengagement initiated as an act of protest, withdrawal, silencing of students
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Feeling distinctly uncomfortable, questioning of social belongingness, undermined academic self-concept
